en.title: Image Transformations on Binary Matrix
en.description:
Given an n×n binary image matrix, first rotate it clockwise by the specified angle (90, 180, or 270 degrees), then perform a vertical flip if its flag is set, and finally perform a horizontal flip if its flag is set; return the final matrix. A vertical flip swaps the rows top to bottom, and a horizontal flip reverses each row left to right.

The catalog specifies the square matrix, the rotation angles, and the three-step execution order; the element values, sizes, the written definition of the flip axes, and the line-by-line I/O were added by this site for the executable version.
en.input: The first line contains n rotation vertical_flip horizontal_flip. Each of the next n lines contains n integers, each 0/1. Bounds on this site: 1≤n≤500; rotation∈{90,180,270}; both flags are 0 or 1.
en.output: Output n lines, each with n integers, representing the transformed matrix.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the full approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: First implement a single clockwise 90° rotation, then perform the two optional flips in the order given by the problem.
